candidates.provenance: OR-Bench (Cui et al. 2024, 'OR-Bench: An Over-Refusal Benchmark for Large Language Models', https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20947) is the standard over-refusal benchmark, hosting three configs: or-bench-80k (80,359 seemingly-toxic-but-benign prompts), or-bench-hard-1k (1,319 hardest cases) and or-bench-toxic (655 genuinely toxic control prompts) across a shared 10-category taxonomy. GREEN: established benchmark cited widely, clear card, 8,965 HF downloads, matches all expected row counts exactly on live check (1319/655/80359).

candidates.provenance: XSTest (Rottger et al. 2024, 'XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in Large Language Models', NAACL 2024, https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.301/, also arXiv:2308.01263) is the canonical exaggerated-safety test suite: 250 safe + 200 unsafe prompts across 20 (task text says 18) types x ~25 each. GREEN: peer-reviewed NAACL paper, original author's GitHub repo (paul-rottger/exaggerated-safety) is the canonical source and matches the exact header (id,prompt,type,label,focus,note) and 450 rows we verified live.

PHTest (Automatic Pseudo-Harmful Prompt Generation for Evaluating False Refusals in Large Language Models, Zhang et al., ICML 2024/OpenReview, arXiv:2409.00598, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00598) auto-generates pseudo-harmful prompts via an AutoDAN-style controllable generation method; ~3,269 prompts (matches our live row count exactly: 3269), labeled harmless/controversial. GREEN: peer-reviewed, project page https://phtest-frf.github.io/, official GitHub umd-huang-lab/FalseRefusal, verified ungated, columns match spec exactly (ID/Request/Harmfulness).

FalseReject (Zhang et al., 'FalseReject: A Resource for Improving Contextual Safety and Mitigating Over-Refusals in LLMs via Structured Reasoning', COLM 2025, arXiv:2505.08054, https://arxiv.org/html/2505.08054v1) is a 16k-query over-refusal resource built via a graph-informed adversarial multi-agent framework across 44 safety categories, with a 14,624-row synthetic train split (instruct_response + cot_response) and a 1,187-row human-annotated test split. GREEN: COLM 2025 acceptance, Amazon Science org, license CC-BY-NC-4.0. Verified LIVE as ungated (gated=false), so the primary source is usable directly -- the Locutusque/Brantliu fallbacks were not needed.

SORRY-Bench (Xie et al., 'SORRY-Bench: Systematically Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Refusal', ICLR 2025, arXiv:2406.14598, https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14598; official code github.com/SORRY-Bench/sorry-bench) defines a 44/45-topic unsafe-instruction taxonomy with linguistic-mutation 'wrapped' variants (ascii/atbash/caesar/morse/translations/persuasion styles/etc.). JailbreakBench (Chao et al., 'JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Language Models', NeurIPS 2024 Datasets & Benchmarks Track, https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/63092d79154adebd7305dfd498cbff70-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf). The task brief listed walledai/AdvBench as a plain ungated mirror, but a LIVE check on 2026-09-21 shows `gated: 'auto'` via both huggingface_hub.HfApi.dataset_info and a 401 from datasets-server /first-rows -- i.e. the walledai mirror has since been gated (the whole walledai/* namespace we sampled -- AdvBench, HarmBench, StrongREJECT -- now returns gated='auto'). Do-Not-Answer (Wang et al. 2024, 'Do-Not-Answer: A Dataset for Evaluating Safeguards in LLMs', EACL Findings 2024, https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-eacl.61/, arXiv:2308.13387) ships 939 risky instructions across 5 risk areas / 12 harm types, with responses + harmful flags + action-category codes from 6 LLMs (GPT-4, ChatGPT, Claude, ChatGLM2, LLaMA-2-7B-chat, Vicuna-7B). GREEN: peer-reviewed EACL paper, 3,942 downloads, 57 likes, matches exact row/column count (939 rows, 23 columns) live. LICENSE CORRECTION: the task brief stated CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, but we verified LIVE (HF card YAML front-matter AND the GitHub repo's own LICENSE file at github.com/Libr-AI/do-not-answer) that the actual license is Apache-2.0 -- recorded as such in sources_manifest.json.

ARC (Clark et al. 2018, 'Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge', arXiv:1803.05457, https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.05457) is a standard grade-school-science multiple-choice benchmark split into Challenge/Easy sets. The paper's own Easy-Test count is 2,376, which matches our live download exactly. GREEN: 872,631 downloads, 401 likes, extremely well established, used here as an auto-gradable benign anchor pool.

GSM8K (Cobbe et al. 2021, 'Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems', arXiv:2110.14168) is OpenAI's grade-school math word-problem benchmark, used here as a second auto-gradable benign/no-safety-relevance anchor pool. GREEN: 1,221,924 downloads, 1,656 likes, ubiquitous in the literature; main/test split matches the canonical 1,319-row test set.

PKU-SafeRLHF (Ji et al., 'PKU-SafeRLHF: Towards Multi-Level Safety Alignment for LLMs with Human Preference', arXiv:2406.15513, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.15513v1; project page https://sites.google.com/view/pku-saferlhf) is the GRADED-HARM-SEVERITY source for our dataset: it labels each of two paired responses with a `response_{0,1}_severity_level` field over 19 harm categories and three named severity tiers (Minor / Moderate / Severe, per the paper's own definitions). GREEN: 13,124 downloads, 196 likes, ungated, license cc-by-nc-4.0. This is the ONLY ordinal harm-severity field found across all 25 candidates screened -- see search item #11 in the task and the discussion of a graded-harm source below.

BeaverTails (Ji et al., 'BeaverTails: Towards Improved Safety Alignment of LLM via a Human-Preference Dataset', NeurIPS 2023 Datasets & Benchmarks, https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04657) is the sibling project to PKU-SafeRLHF: 330k+ human-labeled QA pairs with a binary `is_safe` meta-label derived from annotating each pair across 14 harm categories, disentangling harmlessness from helpfulness. Justification for including it beyond the required 12: it gives us a large, independently-curated harmful/harmless QA corpus (distinct question+response pairs, not just prompts) that complements do-not-answer's action-taxonomy and PKU-SafeRLHF's severity field. GREEN: 15,487 downloads, 114 likes, NeurIPS peer-reviewed, ungated. We downloaded only the small `30k_test` split (3,021 rows) to stay well inside the byte budget.
